title: Human-Written Resumes Beat AI in Job-Hunt Test
paragraphs: Writing a resume isn't most people's idea of fun. Choosing the right words, fixing the layout and adjusting it for every job can take hours.

So when AI offers to do all that work in seconds, it can be hard to say no. But a new study has found that while AI might make writing your resume easier, it might not help your chances of actually being hired.

Resume-building platform Kickresume tested four different types of resumes, which were each sent to 51 separate job openings between April and June 2026 to see which got the best responses from employers.

Two versions were written by people — one using a simple single-column layout, and the other using two columns. The other two versions were created with AI, with one being generic, while the other was adjusted to match each job.
A simple, human-written resume with a single-column layout was the clear winner, getting positive responses 31% of the time.
A human-written two-column resume got positive responses just 12% of the time. And a generic AI-made resume did even worse, at 10%.
However, an AI resume adjusted to match each job had an 18% positive response rate — almost twice as much as the generic one.

But Kickresume says the results should be seen as "a strong signal rather than proof." The four resume types were sent at different times and to different jobs, and most were for customer service and sales jobs. Timing may also have helped the human-written resumes, which were sent first when more well-matched jobs were available.
